hypothesis: M5-T (research_plan_zpd_teacher.md v1.7, Change B): a static one-sided Z-height termination anneal (anchor_pos + ee_body_pos ordinary bounds 0.30 -> 0.15 and low-root adaptive bounds 1.50 -> 0.75 over iters 0-150, trainer=trl_threshold_curriculum) manufactures a difficulty frontier on data where the fixed-threshold control produces none. Activation is the directly instrumented per-iteration fraction of episode ends where anchor_pos or ee_body_pos fired; it must be in [0.15, 0.6] for >= 50% of exact finite iterations 1..200 (classify_m5_activation.py --arm m5_t). The effect screen requires mean MPJPE-G delta <= -0.5 with >= 2/3 seeds improved at a matched fixed strict-vertical 0.15 verifier; eval explicitly sets both vertical thresholds to 0.15 and strips the schedule. Because tracking/eval disables adaptive thresholds, relaxes orientation, and omits foot_pos_xyz, this is not a full release-policy verifier. The 5x low-root/ordinary ratio is invariant during training, so treatment is a uniform 2x -> 1x relaxation of the height-only termination policy. Adaptive sampling stays at the release failure_rate signal in BOTH arms (one axis per arm), and training num_envs exactly equals the frozen dataset motion count so every candidate is active.
